newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GAC to formally adopt postal services common position.
newsitem.headline: GAC to formally adopt postal services common position.

text.p: The European Union's General Affairs Council is set to formally adopt a common position on the draft directive on postal services during its meeting in Luxembourg on Tuesday and Wednesday, EU officials said.
The Council will officially endorse the text agreed by EU telecommunications ministers in December, which would delay any significant liberalisation of the EU's postal sector until at least 2003.
The Council will adopt it as an "A" (non-discussion) point.

The telecoms ministers agreed to allow companies to compete with state post offices to deliver mail weighing more than 350 grammes and costing more than five times that of a standard letter -- a move covering packages and express mail.

However, they decided to wait until at least January 1, 2003 before opening direct mail ("junk mail") and cross-border mail to competition. The formal decision on whether to act would be made before the start of 2000.

Their text, based on COM(95)227, was cleaned up and finalised by COREPER, the EU Committee of Permanent Representatives. Finland, Sweden and the Netherlands -- who all favoured quicker liberalisation -- plan to vote against it, an official said.
The common position now goes to the European Parliament, which has co-decision powers over the directive.
